THE PROBLEM:

Content specialists aren’t the literacy content developers

 • Assessment literacy materials are often an
 afterthought.

 • When they are produced, they often resemble
 textbook material: long and tedious.

 • Assessment content specialists are not web-
 developers (often word documents)
tl;dr
too long; didn’t read

People are busy and
 don’t have time to
 read long articles.

THE VISION:

 For assessment in education to fulfill its potential,
 consumers of assessment results must be able to
 have productive conversations about the results.
 Assessment literacy is the foundation for these
 conversations.

THE VISION:
Assessment literacy materials need to be (and can be)
 user friendly.
 • Web first!!! Utilizing all the web has to offer: pictures,
 video, interactivity, color, …

 • Viewable on multiple devices.

 • Brief, broken into small modules.

 • Sharable via social media, embeddable into other
 web-based content.
Which way to the solution?

GENERAL OBSERVATIONS:

• SEAs are more alike than they are different.

• Effective communication is about establishing a clear
 and consistent vocabulary.

• Great materials produced in one state can be reused/
 repurposed in another.

• The modern web allows content specialists to be
 content developers!

OBSERVATIONS:

 Put 100 assessment specialist in a room and ask them
 about a topic and you’ll hear 150 different points of
view. Our field does not speak with one voice. But that’s
 OK.
